seo.title: Landscaping in Langford, BC | RNC Landscaping
seo.description: Landscape installation, grounds care, irrigation and tree work for Langford homes, stratas and new builds, from Bear Mountain to Happy Valley. Free quote.

intro: Langford is growing fast. We work on new subdivisions in Westhills and Happy Valley, hillside homes on Bear Mountain, townhouse stratas and retail centres, and new-build sites that need landscape installed to drawings.

Langford regulates tree and vegetation removal in development permit areas such as steep slopes, sensitive ecosystems and land near lakes and streams, and its Tree Protection Bylaw applies across the city. See [commercial and contractor work](/commercial/) or [get a free quote](/quote/).
See [sample projects](/portfolio/) and our [seasonal guides](/resources/) for more.

localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

Langford's Tree Protection Bylaw applies across the city. Removing a protected tree on private property needs a Tree Permit (or a Development Permit when part of development); work in designated development permit areas is also regulated, and Parks authorizes all removals on public land and boulevards.

The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.
